facts.text: ASAM's OpenX off-road workshop took place in 2023 and was followed by an off-road concept project.
facts.quote: The OpenX off-road workshop (2023) and the follow-on concept project

facts.text: ASAM's OpenX off-road workshop and follow-on concept project consider construction, mining, agriculture, defence and consumer recreation.
facts.quote: The OpenX off-road workshop (2023) and the follow-on concept project consider construction, mining, agriculture, defence and consumer recreation

facts.text: ASAM's OpenX off-road workshop and follow-on concept project identify mobility as an off-road use case: vehicles moving across diverse and challenging terrains, including uneven surfaces, slopes and obstacles.
facts.quote: mobility ("vehicles are moving across diverse and challenging terrains, including uneven surfaces, slopes, and obstacles")

facts.text: ASAM's OpenX off-road workshop and follow-on concept project identify manipulation as an off-road use case encompassing excavation, lifting, loading, transportation and deposition of materials.
facts.quote: manipulation ("excavation, lifting, loading, transportation, and deposition of materials")

facts.text: ASAM's OpenX off-road workshop and follow-on concept project identify missing OpenX concepts for soft and particle terrain, deformable terrain, vegetation, heavy-machinery manipulation and sensor degradation.
facts.quote: name missing concepts for soft and particle terrain, deformable terrain, vegetation, heavy-machinery manipulation and sensor degradation

facts.text: The identified OpenX off-road gaps do not mean OpenX is unusable; extensions or a manufacturer-owned domain model will be necessary for off-road work.
facts.quote: The correct reading is not that OpenX is unusable but that extensions or a manufacturer-owned domain model will be necessary.

facts.text: The cited ASAM OpenX off-road workshop evidence is standards-body workshop expert opinion, not normative evidence.
